subject: parameters for prior distribution in MAP estimation

messages.author: 7636027d6c15836f
messages.subject: parameters for prior distribution in MAP estimation
parts:
As I understand it, for MAP you assume a prior distribution Φ(Θ) and multiply it with the ML estimation formula.


What parameters does mirt assume for Φ(Θ)?

For instance, does mirt assume a normal Φ(Θ) with mean 0 and sd 1? Or it can somehow attain a more sophisticated knowledge regarding the nature of the prior distribution?


In the documentation I can see the mirt::fscores function, where there is an argument "plausible.type" claiming to perform a normal approximation based on the ACOV matrix (I assume ACOV stands for asymptotic covariance).


Does the "plausible.type" argument has anything to do with the prior distribution estimation Φ(Θ) in the MAP formula above?


If not what are the parameters of Φ(Θ)?




plausible.type

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: parameters for prior distribution in MAP estimation
parts:
On Wed, Oct 31, 2018 at 9:45 AM Dimitrios Zacharatos <sedz...@gmail.com> wrote:

As I understand it, for MAP you assume a prior distribution Φ(Θ) and multiply it with the ML estimation formula.


What parameters does mirt assume for Φ(Θ)?
For instance, does mirt assume a normal Φ(Θ) with mean 0 and sd 1? Or it can somehow attain a more sophisticated knowledge regarding the nature of the prior distribution?

Sure, you can choose different priors. In fact, when fitting a latent regression model these include conditional prediction information to help improve the estimates. In fscores, you can even pass your own prior distribution if you think normal is a bad choice.

In the documentation I can see the mirt::fscores function, where there is an argument "plausible.type" claiming to perform a normal approximation based on the ACOV matrix (I assume ACOV stands for asymptotic covariance).

Yes, and this is the ACOV for each individual response pattern. So, the inverse curvature of the equation you provided.

Phil

Does the "plausible.type" argument has anything to do with the prior distribution estimation Φ(Θ) in the MAP formula above?


If not what are the parameters of Φ(Θ)?




plausible.type
